mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.0% in the month preceding the decision is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 forward return due to reduced risk-free discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.0% in the month prior to decision
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when FEDFUNDS > 5.0% (two-tailed t-test, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) exceeding 10,000 above the prior month's level coincides with a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days as investor risk aversion rises.
failure_condition: In 20 consecutive such trigger events, the 5-day forward return is non-negative in at least 60% of cases (binomial test).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) grows at a double-digit pace month-over-month, it predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days as strong supply-side momentum boosts equity valuations.
regime_hint: Economic expansion with strong manufacturing momentum
failure_condition: Across 5 such high-growth INDPRO months, the 60-day forward return mean is not statistically positive (one-sample t-test, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining retail sales (not directly observable in the catalog, but proxy via HOUST decline) are associated with a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days as market anticipates further contraction.
candidate_trigger: HOUST shows two consecutive monthly declines
failure_condition: In 10 such double-decline HOUST events, the 20-day forward return is not negative in more than 70% of cases (binomial test).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over three consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days as deflation erodes real interest rates.
failure_condition: Over 8 such 3-month CPIAUCSL declines, the 60-day forward return mean is not significantly positive (bootstrap confidence interval includes zero).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 4.5% triggers a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days as elevated labor market friction increases perceived systemic risk.
failure_condition: In 15 such UNRATE > 4.5% events, the 20-day forward return is not negative in more than 50% (binomial test).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in both retail sales (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) by at least 2% month-over-month indicate strong dual demand, which predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > HOUST previous month + 2% AND INDPRO > INDPRO previous month + 2%
failure_condition: Across 8 such interaction events, the 5-day forward return mean is not significantly positive (bootstrap CI includes zero).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in consumer credit (not directly observable, but proxy via a composite of available credit series if available; fallback: use RSAFS as a proxy for credit availability) followed by a rebound in industrial production (INDPRO) within the same month predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days as market anticipates supply-chain normalization.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < RSAFS previous month AND INDPRO > INDPRO previous month + 5%
failure_condition: In 10 such RSAFS-INDPRO interaction events, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (two-tailed t-test, p > 0.05).
